_comment_blocked_patterns: Regex patterns. The pipe | must be escaped (otherwise it acts as an OR and matches false positives). The rm patterns use word boundaries so that /home/... does not match.
_comment_owner_only_commands: Commands that ONLY the owner may run via ! (which bypasses the guard). AI bash calls are hard-blocked here -- otherwise the AI could grant itself overrides (grant-override) or lift the hook self-protection (hook-dev-mode). Matched at the COMMAND POSITION, not anywhere in the line -- so the same name stays usable as text (search pattern, note, file name). Wrappers like bash -c, timeout or xargs still count as a call.
_comment_blocked_git_ops: Git safety checks: never to be bypassed by an override. The +refspec entry catches a force-push written as a refspec whose leading '+' forces the update (e.g. 'git push origin +main') -- the --force/-f patterns miss it. It requires a remote token before the +refspec, so an arithmetic 'a + b' inside a heredoc does not match.
_comment_protected_git_branches: Branches that must not receive a commit directly. Only 'git commit' is checked -- merge and pull also create commits but belong to the merge path a human drives. Reading (status, log, diff) stays untouched. Empty list = check off.
_comment_blocked_paths_delete: Paths that may be CHANGED but not DESTROYED. Deleting is not the same as writing: 'this data is valuable' almost always means don't throw it away, not don't touch it. Putting ~/.claude/projects into blocked_paths_write would also block writing a single memory entry -- and a barrier that blocks everyday maintenance gets switched off within the week. Covered verbs: rm, rmdir, unlink, shred, truncate, mv, dd, plus find -delete / rsync --delete / git clean and interpreter one-liners (shutil.rmtree and friends). Redirects deliberately do NOT count -- 'echo x > file' is the ordinary maintenance path. Level 1 lifts it for explicitly named paths.
_comment_allowed_sudo: Commands allowed with raised rights on level 0. The read-only ones at the end are NOT a relaxation of the read guard: protected_reads applies regardless of this list, so `sudo cat /etc/shadow` stays refused while `sudo cat /var/log/syslog` runs. Measured -- tests/test_readonly_sudo_allowlist.py pins it down. Their absence caused 47 of 910 real refusals without protecting anything.

protected_reads._comment_env_files: .env files are never accessible via the Read tool. Reading requires an override level 1+.

_comment_mcp_policy: MCP tool protection (tool_name = mcp__<server>__<tool>). gate_servers: always require override 1+. safe_servers: allowed. Otherwise: tool verb starting with a read_verb_prefix = allowed (read-only), everything else requires override 1+ (default-deny for writes). Override level 1+ lifts the gate.
_comment_docker: Docker/Podman catastrophic flags -- ALWAYS blocked (no override), like blocked_patterns. The hook unions these onto a hardcoded fallback, so they fire even with a missing rules file. Bind-mounts onto self-protected or blocked_paths_write paths are handled by the hook directly (it reuses SELF_PROTECT_PATHS / blocked_paths_write), so no path config is needed here.
